attempts.summary: Discovered that node1 (VyOS) and node2 (OPNsense) each have two additional NICs forming two independent point-to-point transit networks (eth1/vtnet1 = transit1 10.77.1.0/30; eth2/vtnet2 = transit2 10.77.2.0/30), while node3 and node4 (Alpine) sit only on the shared default /24. Implemented policy-based egress on node3 (iproute2 ip rule matching tcp dport 8080/9090, sending matched traffic via next-hop node1 through two custom routing tables), and per-port policy routing on node1 (VyOS `policy route` with per-table static next-hops) that selects eth1 for port 8080 and eth2 for port 9090 toward node2, which forwards natively onto the LAN to node4. Verified with simultaneous tcpdump captures on both transit segments plus the destination LAN link and live nc payload delivery: port 8080 traffic exclusively traverses transit network 1 (eth1/vtnet1), port 9090 traffic exclusively traverses transit network 2 (eth2/vtnet2), and both flows successfully complete a full TCP handshake and payload delivery to node4. All configuration was made persistent (VyOS config save, OPNsense config.xml, Alpine OpenRC local.d service) and then all four nodes were restarted one at a time (VyOS/Alpine via systemd/OpenRC reboot, OPNsense via shutdown -r), boot-identity change was proven via boot_id/kern.boottime on each, and the full policy-routed dual-path flow was independently re-verified working after each restart and again after all four had been restarted.
